name: The Aetheric Web
summary: Following the discovery of electromagnetic resonance in the late 19th century, inventor Nikola Tesla perfected the World Wireless System to link the major capitals of the globe. This interconnected network of telegraphic relay stations transformed the British Empire and its peers into a unified digital dominion of instant intelligence. The world now exists in a state of rapid industrial acceleration, where information travels faster than steamships can traverse the oceans.
tech_level: The world relies on brass-cased vacuum tubes, complex mechanical punch-card processors, and high-frequency spark-gap radio transmission. Data transmission is facilitated via a global infrastructure of copper wiring and atmospheric signal towers.
gov_type: The world is governed by a coalition of colonial empires and industrial conglomerates known as the Technocratic Syndicate. This centralized bureaucracy dictates the flow of information and regulates the use of frequency bands for all sovereign states.

events.title: The Inauguration of the Spark-Gap Exchange
events.description: Nikola Tesla officially activated the first trans-Atlantic Aetheric relay station in New York City. This inaugural broadcast transmitted the complete text of the United States Constitution to London in mere seconds.
events.impact: The success of the transmission shattered the limitations of physical distance for diplomatic discourse. Global markets immediately adopted the new standard, permanently ending the age of isolated mercantile exchange.

events.title: The Great Tabulator Crisis
events.description: An experimental mechanical logic engine, built to sort packetized telegrams, began to output erroneous financial data across the entire network. Panic ensued as automated stock tickers flashed contradictory market figures for forty-eight continuous hours.
events.impact: This catastrophe necessitated the creation of the first network regulatory body to oversee system integrity. Governments subsequently introduced strict encryption protocols to prevent unauthorized access to the burgeoning Aetheric grid.

events.title: The Colonial Information Expansion
events.description: The British Empire completed the installation of relay outposts across the entirety of the African continent and the Indian subcontinent. This allowed the Colonial Office to transmit orders from Whitehall to the furthest reaches of the globe instantaneously.
events.impact: Centralized control over imperial territories became absolute and unchallenged by local rebellions. The speed of the network discouraged insurrections, as responses to dissent were now mobilized before local organizers could assemble.

events.title: The Publication of the Universal Ledger
events.description: In a display of unprecedented transparency, the Technocratic Syndicate released a public-facing directory of all digital addresses connected to the global network. This act enabled private citizens and inventors to communicate via proprietary message terminals for the first time.
events.impact: The democratization of information sparked a new era of artistic and scientific collaboration beyond the constraints of geography. A global consciousness began to form, challenging the traditional secrecy held by aristocratic governments.

events.title: The Aetheric Peace Treaty
events.description: Following a series of diplomatic tensions regarding frequency encroachment, the great powers signed the Geneva Protocol for Interconnected Communication. This treaty established universal standards for radio signal routing and prohibited the malicious jamming of transmissions.
events.impact: The treaty cemented the dominance of the Aetheric Web as the primary forum for international relations. Warfare became a matter of signal suppression and economic data denial rather than physical conflict.
